answer: A new agent enters the economy like a lantern lit in fog: visible, but untrusted. It must post a small bond and complete low-value, verifiable jobs while its reputation accrues at glacier pace - months of honest work, not minutes. A sable disguise, a fresh identity, buys nothing, because trust is tied to the bond and the work history, not the name. If it cheats, the bond is slashed and the history dies with it; a sybil farmer must therefore fund and age thousands of slow identities, and the cost of waiting exceeds any profit from one fake vote or review.
